title: Certificate data for the cyclic Bell Tsirelson bound

theorem.bell_operator: I_d = sum_{y=0}^{d-1} Re((A_0 + omega^y A_1) tensor B_y), omega = exp(2 pi i/d)
theorem.value: beta_q(I_d) = beta_qa(I_d) = beta_qc(I_d) = 2 csc(pi/(2d)) for every integer d >= 2
theorem.upper_bound_scope: The upper bound holds for arbitrary unitary A_0, A_1, B_0, ..., B_{d-1} satisfying [A_x,B_y]=0; neither the order-d relations nor a tensor-product representation are used.
theorem.lower_bound_scope: The explicit Weyl strategy is d-dimensional and its observables satisfy the required order-d relations.

analytic_upper_certificate.normal_summands: N_y = I + omega^y U is normal because N_y^* N_y = N_y N_y^* = 2I + omega^y U + omega^(-y) U^*
analytic_upper_certificate.polar_sos: If C = V|C| is the polar decomposition (V may be a partial isometry) and B is a commuting unitary, then (|C|+|C^*|)/2 - Re(CB) = P^*P/2, where P = |C^*|^(1/2) - V|C|^(1/2)B.

analytic_lower_certificate.maximizing_spectrum: The spectrum of W consists of all d roots of lambda^d=(-1)^(d-1), hence every eigenvalue is a scalar maximizer.
analytic_lower_certificate.polar_observables: N_y=I+omega^y W, H_y=|N_y|, V_y=Z N_y H_y^(-1), B_y=(V_y^*)^T
analytic_lower_certificate.phase_orientation: With p(z)=(1+z)/|1+z|, B_y^T=Q_y=p(W_y)^* Z^*; the adjoint is essential.
analytic_lower_certificate.source_fourier_constraints: sum_y B_y = alpha_d Z^*, sum_y omega^y B_y = alpha_d X, alpha_d = csc(pi/(2d)), and tau_d = 2 alpha_d.
analytic_lower_certificate.invertibility: Every H_y is invertible: -omega^(-y) is not a root of lambda^d=(-1)^(d-1).
analytic_lower_certificate.order_argument: V_y=Z^y V_0 Z^(-y). In a W-eigenbasis V_0=Z g(W), g(lambda)=(1+lambda)/|1+lambda|, is a cyclic weighted shift. Thus V_0^d=prod_lambda g(lambda) I=I because prod_lambda(1+lambda)=2>0. Hence B_y^d=I.

executable_verification.disclaimer: The executable checks are finite exact symbolic checks and finite floating-point sanity checks. They are not a formal machine proof of the all-dimensional theorem; the all-dimensional result rests on the analytic argument.
exact_symbolic_checks: finite instances d=2,...,12 of the roots-of-unity product polynomial
finite integer parity identities used in the Weyl power calculation
floating_point_checks: random polar SOS identities, including zero and rank-deficient C
complete global SOS certificate for random arbitrary unitaries and varied Alice/Bob dimensions
commuting-operator certificate on direct sums of unequal tensor blocks
scalar bound and every equality root
Weyl commutation, power, spectrum, and functional-calculus equality
unitarity, order d, and complete d-th-root spectrum of every B_y
agreement of the polar B_y with Eqs. (15) and (45) of the originating paper
explicit phase orientation B_y^T = p(W_y)^* Z^*
the two originating Fourier constraints and the explicit d=3 formula
Bell expectation, maximizing eigenvector residual, and top eigenvalue
